svg.title: Fig. 193 — Euler's spiral (the clothoid) with its two asymptotic points
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 193, page 215. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The axes and the origin O. The spiral passes through O and the x-axis is its tangent there.

Euler's spiral: from O the curvature grows in proportion to the arc length s (R·s = a²), so the curve bends more and more, and winds round the point (x0, y0) in the upper right and round (−x0, −y0) in the lower left.
The centres of the two spirals are the asymptotic points (x0, y0) and (−x0, −y0), x0 = y0 = a√π/2: the curve never reaches them but winds in towards them.
